newsitem.title: UK: Freight market subdued, BFI drops 13 points.
newsitem.headline: Freight market subdued, BFI drops 13 points.

text.p: The week started in a subdued fashion in most areas of the freight market, with the Baltic Freight Index slipping 13 points to 1,430 as some panamax rates eased.

Caper conditions were described by brokers as well balanced, although possibly a little weaker in the Atlantic, while grain brokers reported that for panamaxes and handies they saw no serious pressure anywhere.
GRAIN - Sources close to Halla said that it had taken another 25 cents off the last reported U.S. Gulf/Japan rate with 54,000 heavy grain for end March/early April at $24.00 no combo.
There were incomplete reports that Bulfracht had fixed Alam Baru 65,117 dwt open spot Ghent for grain business via U.S. Gulf to Japan.
Little else was reported from the U.S. Gulf for either new fixtures or fresh enquiry for panamaxes or handies.
Reports of panamax business were also lacking from Argentina and Brazil and no further information was available about rumours of Oldendorff covering Plate/Malaysia.
In the handy sizes, Glencore was thought to have covered 35,000 grains 53' Brazil/Lisbon-Hamburg range at a relatively cheap but undisclosed level.
Galaxy was linked with Grigorpan 30,000 dwt for Paranagua/Adriatic grains at about $25.00.

New business quoted today included Toepfer for 55,000 heavy grain Paranagua/Holland and 25,000 heavy grain up River/Ghent-Hamburg range both for March 7/14 and Cabral 2.2/2.6m cft delivery south Brazil March 20/31 trip Continent.
From the continent Halla quoted 50,000 rye to Japan for March/April, and Sigma 13/14,000 wheat Rouen/Canary islands for March.
MINERALS - Some new caper business for Chinese account was introduced to the market today, brokers said.
However, brokers believed the Atlantic might be a little weaker for these types.
NYK confirmed Primo 123,023 dwt delivery Skaw mid March for a trip via Brazil to the Far East at about $13,500 daily.
Nafsika M was booked for 150,000/10 iron ore Saldanha Bay/Beilun for March 20/30 at about $8.00/$8.40 but brokers said the business was completed in the middle of last week.
British Steel was linked with a large panamax for iron ore from Ponta da Madeira to Immingham for prompt loading at close to $7.75.

In the coal trade, talk suggested that Cobelfret may have fixed Timawra 128,370 dwt from Richards Bay to the Continent at under $7.00, and there were also reports that a caper had been fixed for Hampton Roads/Taranto by Italian charterers, although further details were not forthcoming.
HANDY-SIZES - The Pacific continued to be active and firm, although not for smaller geared tonnage and container types.

EACC was said to have booked a 47,000 dwt vessel delivery Far East for a trip via Nopac to south east Asia at $9,650 daily, but the 1,300 teu-capacity Caledonia 25,082 dwt was said to have been fixed by Clan Lin delivery Hong Kong early March for an east coast south America round at only $8,400 daily.
Another container vessel Puerto Cortes 17,993 dwt was linked to Nedlloyd with similar delivery for a west African round voyage at under $9,000 daily.
